why: MOVED 26 -> 34 on 2026-10-19 (Becca). At 26 (sp_end+1) the cassette measurably degraded the signal peptide: tagged p(SP) 0.667 and cleavage-site probability 0.650 against 0.867/0.967 untagged -- the worst of the eight, and the only arm below 0.9 on p(SP). Re-predicting at 26/34/40/46 (canary_rp_1792374944) gives 0.650/0.973/0.950/0.974, so 34 does not merely recover the call, it beats the untagged protein. Chosen over 46, which is OUTSIDE the admissible interval 25-43 entirely, and over 40 because 34 leaves 22 residues to TM1 (57) against 16 and sits in the Gly/Glu-rich 26-45 stretch rather than near the aromatic run 46-55. Disorder percentile 85.3 against 90.5 at 26 by the same three-predictor method -- still deep in disordered sequence. MECHANISM CORRECTED 2026-10-19: this was first explained as SignalP's 70-residue window -- at 26 it holds one native mature residue and 44 of cassette, at 34 it holds nine, so 'buy more native context'. That is FALSIFIED. HEG1 has no p(SP) deficit and ample room, and across 4/12/20 native residues its site probability runs 0.840/0.789/0.859 -- flat and non-monotonic, never nearing its 0.972 native. Twenty residues is more than double what SLC9A3 bought and recovers nothing. AXL, also with no p(SP) deficit, is flat across its whole interval (canary_rp_1792375661). What the three arms say instead: moving the junction recovers a p(SP) DEFICIT and does NOT recover a softened cleavage SITE. SLC9A3 was the only one of the eight with a native p(SP) deficit (0.867) and the only one that improved. Residue count was incidental -- in the first two cases it was perfectly confounded with which axis was degraded. The confound and the separating test are the InterPro session's. The MOVE still stands: 0.650 -> 0.973 and 0.667 -> 1.000 are measurements on this construct. Only the explanation, and any extrapolation from it, were wrong.
